# Astro site code review (2026-02-26 19:02Z)

_**User**_

Do a thorough code review of the Astro site at /Users/felixtorres/.openclaw/workspace/projects/driveway-mechanic/site. This is "The Driveway Mechanic" — an automotive DIY content site.

Review and report on ALL of the following:

1. **Project structure**: src/ layout, pages, components, content, data files. Is it well-organized?
2. **Layout.astro**: Meta tags (title, description, OG, Twitter cards, canonical URLs), favicon, fonts, scripts. Any missing SEO essentials?
3. **All page files in src/pages/**: What routes exist? Are there any 404-prone patterns, broken dynamic routes, or missing pages?
4. **Content (src/content/)**: How many articles exist? Are there any drafts, empty files, placeholder content, or broken frontmatter?
5. **Components**: Are they well-structured? Any unused components, inconsistent patterns, or accessibility issues (missing alt text, ARIA labels, semantic HTML)?
6. **Tailwind config (tailwind.config.mjs)**: Custom theme, colors, fonts — any issues?
7. **astro.config.mjs**: Site URL, integrations, any misconfigurations?
8. **content.config.ts**: Collection schemas — are they correct and complete?
9. **Data files (src/data/)**: YAML files — any broken references, inconsistencies?
10. **Public assets**: What's in public/? Missing favicon, robots.txt, sitemap?
11. **package.json**: Dependencies up to date? Missing useful integrations?
12. **README.md**: Accurate? Useful?

For each area, note: issues/bugs, missing things, improvement opportunities, and anything that looks like placeholder/incomplete content.

Return a detailed structured report covering all findings.

The Driveway Mechanic\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Fix it yourself. Save hundreds.**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA comprehensive automotive DIY and maintenance website built with Astro + MDX, designed to help everyday drivers handle basic car maintenance and repairs in their driveway.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 🚗 What We Cover\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Fix &amp; Troubleshoot**: Symptom-first diagnosis and repair guides\\\\\\\\n- **Maintain &amp; Prevent**: DIY maintenance schedules and how-tos\\\\\\\\n- **Buy &amp; Compare**: Parts and tools buyer guides with affiliate recommendations\\\\\\\\n- **Learn**: Automotive fundamentals and beginner-friendly education\\\\\\\\n- **Seasonal**: Weather-specific prep and maintenance\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 🛠️ Tech Stack\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Framework**: [Astro](https://astro.build/) 5.0\\\\\\\\n- **Content**: MDX with custom automotive components\\\\\\\\n- **Styling**: [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) with custom design system\\\\\\\\n- **TypeScript**: Full type safety throughout\\\\\\\\n- **Deployment**: Vercel (zero-config)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 🏗️ Architecture\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis site mirrors [The Home Field Guide](https://thehomefieldguide.com/) architecture but is adapted for automotive content:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\nsrc/\\\\\\\\n├── components/mdx/          # Safety warnings\\\\\\\\n│   ├── ToolsParts.astro     # Required tools and parts lists\\\\\\\\n│   ├── VehicleFitment.astro # Vehicle compatibility badges\\\\\\\\n│   ├── OBDCode.astro        # OBD-II code explanations\\\\\\\\n│   └── CostComparison.astro # Base layout\\\\\\\\n│   └── Article.astro       # Article layout with automotive features\\\\\\\\n└── pages/                  # Static and dynamic routes\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 🚀 Getting Started\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Prerequisites\\\\\\\\n- Node.js 18+ \\\\\\\\n- npm or yarn\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Installation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Clone the repository**\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\n   git clone https://github.com/username/driveway-mechanic.git\\\\\\\\n   cd driveway-mechanic\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Install dependencies**\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\n   npm install\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Start development server**\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\n   npm run dev\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n4. **Build for production**\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\n   npm run build\\\\\\\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 📝 Content Creation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Article Types\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Troubleshooting**: &#96;fix/car-wont-start-clicks&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **How-to Maintenance**: &#96;maintain/how-to-change-oil-toyota-camry&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Buyer Guides**: &#96;buy/best-obd2-scanners-2026&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Cost Guides**: &#96;fix/brake-job-cost&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Comparisons**: &#96;buy/ceramic-vs-semi-metallic-brake-pads&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Frontmatter Schema\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\ntitle: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"How to Change Oil on a 2018-2023 Toyota Camry\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\npillar: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"maintain\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"          # States\\\":{},\\\"selfSummaryCount\\\":0,\\\"readPaths\\\":[]},\\\"text\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"toolFormerData\\\":{\\\"toolCallId\\\":\\\"tool_08fef692-1f78-43a7-ab14-50e11260855\\\",\\\"toolIndex\\\":0,\\\"modelCallId\\\":\\\"tool_08fef692-1f78-43a7-ab14-50e11260855\\\",\\\"status\\\":\\\"completed\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"read_file_v2\\\",\\\"rawArgs\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"path\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/Users/felixtorres/.openclaw/workspace/projects/driveway-mechanic/site/src/content/articles/car-wont-start-clicks.mdx\\\\\\\"}\\\",\\\"tool\\\":40,\\\"params\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"targetFile\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/Users/felixtorres/.openclaw/workspace/projects/driveway-mechanic/site/src/content/articles/car-wont-start-clicks.mdx\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"charsLimit\\\\\\\":1000000,\\\\\\\"effectiveUri\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/Users/felixtorres/.openclaw/workspace/projects/driveway-mechanic/site/src/content/articles/car-wont-start-clicks.mdx\\\\\\\"}\\\",\\\"result\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"contents\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\\ntitle: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Car Won't Start but Clicks: What to Check First\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nexcerpt: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Your car clicks when you turn the key but won't start? This usually points to a dead or weak battery, bad connections, or a failing starter. Here's how to diagnose and fix it yourself.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\npublishedAt: 2026-02-10\\\\\\\\nauthor: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The Driveway Mechanic Team\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nhubs: [\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"electrical\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\ncategory: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\narticleType: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"troubleshooting\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nvehicles: [\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"all\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\ndifficulty: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"beginner\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ntimeCostSkill:\\\\\\\\n  time: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"15–30 min\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  diyCost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$0–$150\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  shopCost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$75–$300\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  skill: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"beginner\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  notes: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Most fixes are simple and require basic tools\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nsafetyLevel: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"low\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\npartsNeeded: [\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"jumper-cables\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"battery-terminal-cleaner\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"new-battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\ntoolsNeeded: [\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"multimeter\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"wrench-set\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"wire-brush\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\nobdCodes: []\\\\\\\\ntopics: [\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"starter\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"electrical\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"troubleshooting\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\nseo:\\\\\\\\n  description: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Car clicks but won't start? Learn how to diagnose dead battery, bad connections, or starter problems. Step-by-step DIY troubleshooting guide with costs.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport FixFlow from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/FixFlow.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport SafetyCallout from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/SafetyCallout.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport ToolsParts from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/ToolsParts.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport Callout from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/Callout.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport CostComparison from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/CostComparison.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport AffiliateProduct from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/mdx/AffiliateProduct.astro\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen you turn the key and hear clicking but your car won't start, you're dealing with one of the most common automotive problems. The good news? **This is usually a simple fix you can handle yourself.**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThat clicking sound is your starter trying to engage but not getting enough power to turn the engine. In 90% of cases, it's either a dead battery, corroded connections, or a failing starter.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Quick Answer\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Most likely causes:**\\\\\\\\n1. **Dead or weak battery** (70% of cases)\\\\\\\\n2. **Corroded battery terminals** (15% of cases)\\\\\\\\n3. **Bad starter** (10% of cases)\\\\\\\\n4. **Loose connections** (5% of cases)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;SafetyCallout \\\\\\\\n  severity=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"warning\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  bullets={[\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Always wear safety glasses when working around batteries\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Remove jewelry to avoid short circuits\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Never smoke or use open flames near batteries\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Use proper jack stands if you need to go under the car\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n/&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Diagnostic Steps\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;FixFlow \\\\\\\\n  title=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Find the Problem in Order\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  intro=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Check these in sequence — easiest and most common first:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  steps={[\\\\\\\\n    {\\\\\\\\n      title: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Check Battery Connections\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      details: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Look at both battery terminals for white/green corrosion, loose clamps, or frayed wires.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      outcome: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Clean, tight connections with no visible corrosion\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfPass: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Move to step 2\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfFail: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Clean terminals with baking soda and water, tighten clamps\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n    },\\\\\\\\n    {\\\\\\\\n      title: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Test Battery Voltage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      details: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Use a multimeter to check battery voltage. Should be 12.6V with engine off, 12.0V or higher when cranking.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      outcome: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Voltage reading above 12.4V\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfPass: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Move to step 3\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfFail: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Jump start or replace battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n    },\\\\\\\\n    {\\\\\\\\n      title: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Try Jump Starting\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      details: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Connect jumper cables properly (positive to positive, negative to ground) and attempt to start.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      outcome: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Car starts immediately with jump\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfPass: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Battery is dead — needs charging or replacement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfFail: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Likely starter problem — move to step 4\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n    },\\\\\\\\n    {\\\\\\\\n      title: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Check Starter Connections\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\n      details: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Locate starter (usually on engine block) and check for loose or corroded connections.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      outcome: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"All connections tight and clean\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfPass: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Starter motor likely failed\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n      nextIfFail: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Clean and tighten starter connections\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n  whenToCallPro=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"If all connections are good and jump starting doesn't work, the starter motor likely needs replacement. This requires lifting the car and working with heavy parts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n/&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Tools &amp; Parts You'll Need\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;ToolsParts \\\\\\\\n  mustHave={[\\\\\\\\n    { name: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Multimeter\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", description: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"For testing battery voltage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" },\\\\\\\\n    { name: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Wire brush or sandpaper\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", description: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Clean corroded terminals\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" },\\\\\\\\n    { name: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Adjustable wrench\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", description: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Tighten battery clamps\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" }\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n  niceToHave={[\\\\\\\\n    { name: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Jumper cables or jump starter\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", description: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"For testing and emergency starts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" }\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n/&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Step-by-Step Solutions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Clean Corroded Battery Terminals\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf you see white, blue, or green buildup on your battery terminals:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Disconnect the negative terminal first** (black cable)\\\\\\\\n2. **Disconnect the positive terminal** (red cable)  \\\\\\\\n3. **Mix baking soda and water** (1 tablespoon per cup)\\\\\\\\n4. **Pour mixture over terminals** and let it foam for 30 seconds\\\\\\\\n5. **Scrub with wire brush** until terminals are shiny\\\\\\\\n6. **Rinse with clean water** and dry completely\\\\\\\\n7. **Reconnect positive first, then negative**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;Callout tone=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tip\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\n  Apply terminal protectant spray or petroleum jelly to clean terminals to prevent future corrosion.\\\\\\\\n&lt;/Callout&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Jump Start Your Car\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf the battery is weak but connections are clean:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Position jump car** close enough for cables to reach both batteries\\\\\\\\n2. **Turn off both vehicles** and engage parking brakes\\\\\\\\n3. **Connect cables in this order:**\\\\\\\\n   - Red to dead battery positive\\\\\\\\n   - Red to good battery positive  \\\\\\\\n   - Black to good battery negative\\\\\\\\n   - Black to unpainted metal in dead car (ground point)\\\\\\\\n4. **Start the good car** and let it run for 5 minutes\\\\\\\\n5. **Try starting the dead car**\\\\\\\\n6. **Remove cables in reverse order** once running\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. Test and Replace Battery\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf jump starting works but the problem returns:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;CostComparison \\\\\\\\n  title=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Battery Replacement: DIY vs Shop\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  diyCost=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$100–$150\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  shopCost=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$200–$300\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  diyTime=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"15 minutes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  shopTime=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"30 minutes + wait time\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  diyDescription=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Buy battery at auto parts store, install yourself\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  shopDescription=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Shop tests, purchases, and installs new battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n  breakdownDIY={[\\\\\\\\n    { item: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"New battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", cost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$100–$150\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" },\\\\\\\\n    { item: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Tools\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", cost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Already own\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" }\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n  breakdownShop={[\\\\\\\\n    { item: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"New battery\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", cost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$120–$180\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" },\\\\\\\\n    { item: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Labor\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", cost: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"$80–$120\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" }\\\\\\\\n  ]}\\\\\\\\n/&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**To replace the battery:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Buy the correct battery** (check your owner's manual for group size)\\\\\\\\n2. **Remove old battery** (negative first, then positive)\\\\\\\\n3. **Clean battery tray** if corroded\\\\\\\\n4. **Install new battery** (positive first, then negative)\\\\\\\\n5. **Apply terminal protectant**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;Callout tone=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"note\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\n  Most auto parts stores will test your battery for free and dispose of your old one.\\\\\\\\n&lt;/Callout&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## When the Starter is the Problem\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf jump starting doesn't work and connections are clean, you likely have a bad starter. Signs include:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Single loud click when turning key\\\\\\\\n- Nothing happens (no click at all)\\\\\\\\n- Grinding noise when trying to start\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Starter replacement typically costs:**\\\\\\\\n- **DIY:** $150–$300 (parts only)\\\\\\\\n- **Shop:** $400–$800 (parts + labor)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis job requires lifting the car and working with heavy parts. Unless you're experienced, this is often worth having a shop handle.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Prevention Tips\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;Callout tone=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tip\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\n  Keep your battery healthy: test voltage monthly during cold weather, clean terminals every 6 months, don't leave lights on when the engine is off, drive regularly, and replace every 3–5 years depending on climate and usage.\\\\\\\\n&lt;/Callout&gt;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Related Problems\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf your car has other symptoms along with the clicking:\\\\\\\\n- **Lights are dim:** Definitely a battery issue\\\\\\\\n- **Radio/electronics don't work:** Battery is completely dead\\\\\\\\n- **Car cranks slowly then clicks:** Weak battery or bad connections\\\\\\\\n- **No click at all:** Could be ignition switch, neutral safety switch, or completely dead battery\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Recommended Products\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&lt;AffiliateProduct \\\\\\\\n  name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"NOCO Genius G3500 # The Driveway Mechanic — Full Site Code Review

## 1. Project Structure

**Verdict: Well-organized, mirrors a proven architecture.**

```
site/

│   ├── content/hubs/         # EMPTY
│   ├── data/authors/         # 1 author YAML
│   ├── data/categories/      # 2 category YAMLs
│   ├── data/topics/          # EMPTY

│   ├── pages/                # 7 page files
│   └── styles/global.css
```

**Issues:**
- No `src/lib/` directory despite `tsconfig.json` defining a `@/lib/*` alias
- Empty data directories (`topics/`, `vehicles/`) — schemas defined but no data files exist
- Empty `hubs/` content directory — schema defined, build warns about it
- All 18 components live in `src/components/mdx/` — no top-level reusable UI components (e.g., Button, Card)

## 2. Layout.astro — SEO & Meta Tags

**Verdict: Solid foundation with several gaps.**

**Present:**
- `<meta charset>`, `<meta viewport>`, dynamic `<title>`, `<meta description>`
- Conditional `<link rel="canonical">` and `<meta robots noindex>`
- Open Graph: `og:type`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:site_name`
- Twitter: `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`
- `<link rel="icon">` pointing to `/favicon.svg`
- `<link rel="sitemap">` to `/sitemap-index.xml`
- Mobile menu with proper `aria-label` and `aria-expanded`

**Missing (SEO issues):**
- **`og:image`** — No default OG image. Social sharing will show no preview image.
- **`og:url`** — Missing. Facebook/LinkedIn need this for proper sharing.
- **`twitter:image`** — No Twitter card image.
- **`twitter:site`** / `twitter:creator` — No Twitter handle associated.
- **Structured data (JSON-LD)** — No schema.org markup at all. For an automotive content site, `Article`, `HowTo`, `FAQPage`, and `BreadcrumbList` schemas would significantly boost SEO.
- **Google Fonts preconnect without import** — Lines preconnect to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com` but no fonts are actually loaded. Dead weight.

**Footer typo (minor):**

```133:133:src/layouts/Layout.astro
        <div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:6 lg:px-8 py-12">
```

`sm:6` is not a valid Tailwind class — should be `sm:px-6`.

**That's 14+ broken links from the navigation, homepage, fix index, and footer.**

### Critical Bug: `.mdx` in Generated URLs

The build output reveals all article URLs contain the `.mdx` extension:

```
/buy/best-obd2-scanners-2026.mdx/index.html
/fix/car-wont-start-clicks.mdx/index.html
/fix/check-engine-light-on.mdx/index.html
/maintain/how-to-change-oil-toyota-camry.mdx/index.html
```

This is because the `[...slug].astro` pages use `entry.id` directly as the slug parameter. In Astro 5's Content Layer API with `glob()`, `entry.id` includes the file extension. Every page link to an article (e.g., `/fix/car-wont-start-clicks`) will 404 because the actual URL is `/fix/car-wont-start-clicks.mdx`.

**Fix:** Strip the extension in all three dynamic route files:

```javascript
params: { slug: entry.id.replace(/\.mdx?$/, '') },
```

### Homepage Broken Link: OBD2 Scanners

The homepage links to `/buy/best-obd2-scanners` but the article file is `best-obd2-scanners-2026.mdx`. Even after fixing the `.mdx` extension bug, the slug would be `best-obd2-scanners-2026`, not `best-obd2-scanners`. This link will 404.

## 5. Components

**Verdict: Strong automotive-specific component library with some accessibility gaps.**

18 components in `src/components/mdx/`, all TypeScript-typed. Highlights:

**Well-built:**
- `SafetyCallout` — uses `role="alert"`, severity levels
- `DifficultyMeter` — uses `role="meter"` with ARIA attributes
- `CostComparison` — clean DIY vs shop comparison
- `DiagnosticFlow` / `FixFlow` — step-by-step with pass/fail branching
- `OBDCode` — automotive-specific with severity and "can I keep driving?" info

**Accessibility issues:**
- `GoChecklist` — checkboxes lack `id`/`name` and aren't associated with `<label>` elements
- `TorqueSpec` — data table missing `<caption>` element
- Decorative SVGs across components missing `aria-hidden="true"`
- `GoChecklist` uses inline `onclick` handler for print button

**Potentially unused components** (not imported in any current article):
- `VideoEmbed`
- `RecallCheck`
- `PartNumber`

These may be intended for future content, but right now they're dead code.

**Inconsistency:** `DiagnosticFlow` and `FixFlow` are nearly identical in structure (both have steps with pass/fail) but with different color schemes (amber vs blue). Could be consolidated or at minimum documented when to use which.

**Issue:** The font stack in `tailwind.config.mjs` defines system fonts, but the layout also preconnects to Google Fonts without loading anything. Pick one approach:
- Use system fonts (current config) and remove the Google Fonts preconnect
- Or actually import a Google Font

**Dark mode** is configured (`class` strategy) but there's no dark mode toggle in the UI. CSS variables for `.dark` are defined in Layout.astro but users have no way to activate dark mode.
